pairs.subject: trailer-structure
pairs.evidence: lib/script/trailer/rules/promises.ts:21 The rule files are written to the techniques' own 'in a tool' rules: every promise must name a payer, budget allowances are checked, rungs must declare one raised variable, resets are counted and placed on cue boundaries, and drops must follow the drop order, while anything that needs judgement is reported as unmeasured rather than passed.

techniques.evidence: lib/script/trailer/rules/promises.ts:21 A promise with no payer, or graded unpaid, becomes a finding. A spend is reported as unmeasured. Extraction completeness and promises made by register are an explicit unmeasured row. 'promise' is in ADVISORY_RULES (params.json advisoryRules), so it is never a gate.

lib/script/trailer/rules/withholding.ts:38 Hold and imply-only assets that are spent are violations, and a spend with no recorded trade is a violation. A missing budget is reported as 'undecided', not clean. Campaign drift is honestly unmeasured because the rule sees one cut.

lib/script/trailer/rules/cue.ts:61 Rejects a cue with no breath before its peak and checks that movement and beat cue marks exist. types.ts makes the cue a field of the cut that movements point into. A cut with no cue is unmeasured, not a violation (cue.ts:19), which covers the unscored exemption.

lib/script/trailer/rules/reset.ts:41 No reset is a violation and three or more is a violation. The reset must sit immediately before the single peak, hold one thing and land on a cue boundary. A mood-led cut and a declared drop are not engaged.

lib/script/trailer/rules/escalation.ts:49 The raised variable is an explicit field. Zero or more than one raised variable is a violation, and so is a variable repeated in consecutive rungs. A mood-led cut is not engaged. The last-rung-is-largest check lives in magnitude.ts behind an injected resolver.
lib/script/trailer/rules/ladder.ts:64 Dropped parts must be a prefix of DROP_ORDER, and a long cut with drops is a violation. Part counts per rung are deliberately unmeasured.

pairs.registryProposal: concealment-and-its-tells has no 'in a tool' decision rule, unlike cue-first-assembly, escalation-without-mechanism and promise-ledger. Its own tell forbids a duration threshold, so a checker can only emit an unmeasured row. The technique should say which record a tool must keep (the declared concealment mode per segment, or a feel-of-use signal) so that an unmeasured stub can be told apart from a missing technique.

pairs.subject: trailer-structure
pairs.evidence: lib/cut/deriveTimeline.ts:271 The derived cut's music lane is attached after the picture: each cue's span is derived from the scenes it covers, and the clock comes from beat and shot timecodes. For trailer projects (the file states that a unit is 'an explainer beat or a trailer SHOT') this is the inverted dependency cue-first-assembly names, a tool where beats carry timings and music is attached afterwards.

techniques.evidence: lib/cut/deriveTimeline.ts:271 Music cues are computed from picture.scenes (the header at lines 31-34 says 'A spot's span is DERIVED from the scenes it covers'). lib/score/spots.ts likewise places movements by beat 'at' timecodes because CueSection carries no durations. The technique says the cue must be the timeline's parent. The voice-track exemption covers explainers but not the trailer shots this file also lays out.
